title: Reductive pair (G', G) and the apartment A
body_html:
Reductive pair $(G', G)$ and the apartment $A$

Standing data for the construction of the generalized building:

  • $(G', G)$ is a pair of (connected) reductive groups over a local field $F$, with $G' \le G$ a closed subgroup;
  • $S$ is a maximal $F$-split torus of $G'$, and $N := N(G', S)$ is its normalizer in $G'$;
  • $A \subseteq \mathcal{B}(G')$ is the apartment of the (extended) Bruhat–Tits building of $G'$ corresponding to $S$.

For each point $x \in A$, the parahoric subgroup $G'_x$ of $G'$ attached to $x$ is defined as in Bruhat–Tits theory (it agrees with $G'(\mathcal{O})$ modulo $G_{x,0+}$ for an appropriate integral structure).

The pair $(G', G)$ is the basic raw material from which §5 builds the generalized building $\BSigma$ (see Generalized building B(Σ) = G ×^K A).
